newsitem.title: UK: PacifiCorp outlines bid impact on gearing.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp outlines bid impact on gearing.

text.p: PacifiCorp's planned takeover of Britain's biggest electricity distributor The Energy Group should lift the U.S.-based group's gearing to 67 percent, taking into account planned asset sales, chief financial officer Richard O'Brien said.
O'Brien told a news conference Pacificorp's debt to capitalisation ratio at the end of 1996 was 56 percent.
PacifiCorp has four financing facilities to raise funds for the 3.7 billion stg bid, which also carries $3.8 billion of gross debt in The Energy Group.
One of these facilities is non-investment grade, O'Brien said, accounting for some $1.5 billion of a total funding just over $8 billion.
O'Brien said further asset sales could include parts of the company's financial services unit and independent power company.
"There are significant other assets which we want to dispose of...in the very near future," he said. But he ruled out any sale of Energy's assets in Britain.

O'Brien declined to put a figure on potential cost savings from the proposed merger but said PacifiCorp thought generation costs could be cut in Britain by using expertise and technology from its U.S. business.
In the U.S., he saw benefits from Energy's experience in liberalised, competitive markets.
"We don't have any overlaps...we are not impressing cost reductions at all," he said.
